patient.name: Eleanor Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Weakness and confusion, poor oral intake for several days

history.hpi: Daughter called 911 after finding her mother more confused than usual, weak, and reporting she has barely eaten or had anything to drink for the past 3 days due to nausea. Patient has felt feverish on and off. Skin is dry with poor turgor. No vomiting or diarrhea reported, but patient does report burning with urination for the past two days.
history.lastOralIntake: A few sips of water this morning; no solid food in over 24 hours
history.events: Daughter visited for a scheduled check-in and found her mother confused and weak, called 911 immediately

scene.location: Single-story home, patient found in a recliner in the living room, daughter present
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted; home is cluttered but passable
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, reports mother has been declining for several days; no other family on scene
visualCues: Patient appears thin and frail, skin tenting visible on forearms
Dry, cracked lips and dry mucous membranes
Multiple prior bruises and thin, fragile-appearing skin on both arms
Empty water glass on side table, untouched sandwich from earlier in the day
Patient slow to respond to questions, repeats herself

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 78-year-old female with altered mental status, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, and tachycardia. She is oriented to person only and slow to answer questions.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but weak and rapid, skin dry and tenting
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact but generalized weakness noted in all extremities
otherFindings: Oriented to person only, slow and confused responses
Skin tenting present on forearms and sternum
Reports burning with urination for two days
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I'm just... so tired. I don't know what day it is."

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes signs of distributive shock from a likely urinary source and begins vascular access attempts, targeting fluid resuscitation.

phases.name: Vascular access attempted
phases.description: Crew attempts peripheral IV access on fragile, dehydrated veins. Two attempts fail due to poor vein quality and hypovolemia; over 90 seconds elapses without successful access.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew begins peripheral IV attempts given clinical suspicion for septic shock from a urinary source. Fragile, dehydrated veins and poor perfusion make peripheral access difficult; per protocol, failure to obtain access within two attempts or 90 seconds indicates IO placement.

otherFindings: Two peripheral IV attempts unsuccessful — veins collapse on cannulation
Over 90 seconds elapsed since first attempt
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I'm sorry, I know I'm a hard stick..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize signs of distributive (septic) shock: AMS, tachycardia, hypotension for age
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Signs of poor perfusion (due to a medical cause) such as one or more of the following: Altered mental status ... Hypotension for age (lowest acceptable systolic blood pressure in mmHg): Greater than 10 years old: 90
expectedActions.rationale: Early recognition of shock drives the urgency of vascular access and fluid resuscitation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Place IO needle after 2 failed peripheral IV attempts / over 90 seconds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Protocol-directed threshold prevents prolonged delay of fluid resuscitation in shock.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose; correct if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood sugar, and correct if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out hypoglycemia as a contributor to altered mental status.

transitions.condition: After the second failed peripheral attempt exceeds the 90-second threshold, crew places an IO needle and initiates a pressure-infused fluid bolus toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg.
Crew continues attempting peripheral IV access beyond the two-attempt/90-second threshold instead of escalating to IO, delaying fluid resuscitation.

phases.name: IO placed, fluid bolus started
phases.description: IO access is obtained and a pressure-infused isotonic fluid bolus is administered toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg. Vital signs begin to trend toward improved perfusion.
phases.triggerCondition: IO needle successfully placed after the peripheral access threshold was met; crew begins rapid, predetermined fluid boluses per the Shock protocol's MAP-goal-directed fluid resuscitation.

otherFindings: IO access secured in proximal tibia
500 mL isotonic bolus infusing under pressure
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That pinched, but I already feel a little more with it."

expectedActions.shortAction: Isotonic fluid bolus 500 mL pressure-infused via IO over <15 min toward MAP goal 65 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops. Physiologic target: MAP goal 65 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Aggressive early fluid resuscitation is essential for suspected septic shock.

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance notification to receiving hospital for suspected sepsis
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide advanced notification to the hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving facility to prepare for early sepsis management.

transitions.condition: After the first fluid bolus, blood pressure and mental status improve; crew reassesses and continues toward the 30 mL/kg fluid goal while transporting.

phases.name: MAP improves toward goal
phases.description: Perfusion improves following IO fluid resuscitation. Mental status clears further and vital signs trend toward normal as the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.
phases.triggerCondition: Serial reassessment following the fluid bolus shows improving blood pressure, heart rate, and mental status, consistent with a positive response to fluid resuscitation for septic shock.

otherFindings: Oriented to person, place, and situation
Advance notification given to receiving hospital
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel much clearer now, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and mental status serially en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Serial reassessment confirms ongoing response to treatment and guides further fluid administration.

phases.name: Peripheral attempts continue past threshold
phases.description: Crew continues attempting peripheral IV access well beyond the 90-second/two-attempt threshold. Fluid resuscitation is delayed, and the patient's perfusion continues to worsen.
phases.triggerCondition: Repeated peripheral IV attempts continue past the protocol threshold for IO placement, delaying fluid resuscitation. Mental status and blood pressure worsen as hypoperfusion progresses.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak, thready pulses, delayed capillary refill
otherFindings: Four failed peripheral attempts, over 4 minutes elapsed

expectedActions.shortAction: Abandon further peripheral attempts; place IO needle immediately and start fluid bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Continued delay in obtaining access worsens hypoperfusion; the protocol threshold exists to prevent this deterioration.
